checks.label: 1 cm = 10 mm. 1 cm² = 10 mm x 10 mm = 100 mm². Conversion factor is 100: the 1 cm square is drawn as 10 rows of 10 mm squares and counted to 100 mm²; so the 20 cm² plate is 20 × 100 = 2,000 mm², the same as 50 mm × 40 mm, and a 25 mm² conductor is 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 cm²

A common misconception would be that 100 cm² are needed because 1 metre is 100 centimetres: the 1 m square's one row of cm squares along the bottom is 100 cm², a hundredth of it, and its 100 rows make 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm²; the 6 m² floor is 60,000 cm², and the 600 cm² slip is drawn as a red square a hundredth of that

Conductor cross-section 1.5 mm² 2.5 mm² 4 mm² 6 mm² 10 mm² 16 mm² 25 mm² 35 mm²: the cable screen steps through exactly these sizes in this order, each tinting that many of the 100 one-millimetre squares in 1 cm², and ends at 35 mm² = 35 ÷ 100 = 0.35 cm²

IEC 60228 specifies the nominal cross-sectional areas, in the range 0,5 mm2 to 3 500 mm2: every conductor size the lesson uses, the eight listed and the 25 mm² puzzle, lies in that range and is given as an area in mm²

Every side k times as long fits k × k copies: k × k copies of the 10 cm square tile the square k × 10 cm a side exactly (k = 1 to 4), and k × k copies of the triangle, k(k + 1) ÷ 2 upright and k(k − 1) ÷ 2 turned round, each the same size and shape, fill the triangle k times as big (k = 1 to 3); so twice the sides is 4 times the area and the 600 cm² plate tripled is 9 × 600 = 5,400 cm²

Each puzzle's answer is worked out from its rule: 20 × 100 = 2,000 mm²; 6 × 10,000 = 60,000 cm²; a 20 cm square, 4 copies of the 10 cm one; 9 × 600 = 5,400 cm²; 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 cm²; 1,000 × 1,000 = 1,000,000 mm²; 30 × 5 = 150 mm² and 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5 cm², the same as 3 cm × 0.5 cm

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and each wrong answer it names is the one a slip gives: the length's factor (× 10, × 100, ÷ 10) used for an area, a divide for a multiply or a multiply for a divide, × 1,000 for m² to cm², the cm² number for mm², mm² read as cm², the side made 4 times as long, the area made only 3 times or 3 + 3 times as much; each is shown in the warning colour

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: the plate not ruled in mm, the floor not split into cm, the big square's area shown as ?, no copies in the big triangle, no blocks or cm² named beside the conductor, the metre square not tinted, the bar not ruled in cm; no answer anywhere and nothing in the warning colour
Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture and clear of each other and of the lines, for every answer, right or wrong, and at every size the corners can be dragged to

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart; and, filmed 30 frames a second, no readout or label changes in place sooner than 0.2 s after its last change, and no readout appears outside a fade (part() or swap()) unless it is there as the screen opens
